documents.title: Analytics Portal Solution Design
documents.description: Logical solution design for the fersc Analytics Portal, covering the platform roles of Oracle Analytics Cloud, Databricks Lakehouse, and the Confluent iPaaS orchestration layer, with a sequence diagram illustrating the end-to-end data flow from CC&B to business user.
documents.scope: Analytics Portal — the self-service BI surface and underlying data pipeline from Oracle CC&B through Confluent and Databricks to Oracle Analytics Cloud.

executive-summary.summary: The Analytics Portal delivers governed, near-real-time self-service analytics by joining Oracle Analytics Cloud, a Databricks Lakehouse, and a Confluent event backbone over Oracle CC&B operational data.
points: Oracle Analytics Cloud (PLAT-BI) is the self-service BI and reporting surface, connected to the lakehouse via a Databricks SQL endpoint (JDBC).
The Databricks Lakehouse (PLAT-DATA-LAKEHOUSE) is the governed storage and transformation tier; Unity Catalog enforces row- and column-level security per role.
The Confluent iPaaS (PLAT-EVENT-BROKER) moves CC&B data into the lakehouse in near-real-time via change-data-capture.
Scheduled batch ingestion supplements the event-driven flows for MDM and ERP source systems.

context.title: CIS to Data Lakehouse — Billing Ingestion Specification

capabilities.note: Retail & Billing — operational billing KPIs surfaced through the portal.
Customer Management — operational dashboards for contact centre and field teams.
Regulatory & Compliance — Ofgem settlement and RIIO-ED2 reporting datasets.

functional-requirements.requirement: Provide self-service workbooks, subject areas, dashboards, and natural-language querying for operational and commercial business users.
Surface CC&B operational data in the gold layer for reporting without exposing raw PII to analytics users.
Supplement event-driven ingestion with scheduled batch ingestion for MDM and ERP source systems.

features.name: Operational Dashboard
features.description: Near-real-time operational KPI dashboard (DSO, payment failure rate, unread meter percentage) for contact centre and field operations.

features.name: Governed Self-Service BI
features.description: Semantic model of governed metrics, KPIs, and dimensions with role-aware access via Unity Catalog.

features.name: Near-Real-Time Ingestion
features.description: Change-data-capture pipeline delivering CC&B changes to the lakehouse within minutes.

nfr-business-continuity.requirement: The end-to-end pipeline (PLAT-CIS → PLAT-EVENT-BROKER → PLAT-DATA-LAKEHOUSE) must achieve 99.5% availability during business hours (07:00–22:00 UK time).
nfr-business-continuity.rationale: Operational dashboards are used by contact centre and field operations teams throughout the business day.

nfr-data-classification.requirement: PII fields (customer name, address, contact details) must be masked at the Confluent transformation layer and must not be present in Databricks bronze or silver tables. Gold-layer tables may surface pseudonymised identifiers only.
nfr-data-classification.rationale: UK GDPR data minimisation principle. Databricks analytics users should not have access to raw PII.

nfr-performance.requirement: CC&B operational data must be available in the gold layer of the Databricks Lakehouse within 15 minutes of the originating transaction being committed in Oracle CC&B.
nfr-performance.rationale: Reduce operational information lag from 24 hours to under 15 minutes for critical operational KPIs.

nfr-performance.requirement: The Confluent cluster and Databricks Auto Loader must handle 3x current peak event volume (150,000 events/hour) without degradation.
nfr-performance.rationale: Smart meter estate is projected to grow from 800,000 to 2.5 million endpoints by 2028, significantly increasing CC&B event volumes.

arch-business.description: The portal serves operational, commercial, and regulatory reporting consumers. Operational users (contact centre, field operations) consume near-real-time KPIs; commercial users consume financial and trading datasets; regulatory users consume Ofgem settlement and RIIO-ED2 datasets.

arch-data.description: The Databricks Lakehouse stores raw (bronze), cleansed (silver), and curated (gold) Delta tables. Unity Catalog provides governance, lineage, and access control across three catalogues: ops_catalogue (operational datasets), commercial_catalogue (commercial and financial datasets), and regulatory_catalogue (Ofgem settlement and RIIO-ED2 datasets). Gold-layer tables are exposed to OAC via the Databricks SQL serverless endpoint.

arch-integration.description: Oracle CC&B changes are captured by a Debezium Oracle CDC connector (LogMiner) and published to Confluent Kafka. A Kafka Streams processor applies PII masking before Databricks Auto Loader consumes events and lands them in the bronze layer. Scheduled connectors orchestrate batch ingestion for MDM and ERP.

references.note: PLAT-CIS → iPaaS — Avro CDC, events within 60s of DB commit, up to 50,000 events/hour at peak.
iPaaS → PLAT-DATA-LAKEHOUSE — Databricks Auto Loader, micro-batches every 10 minutes.
PLAT-DATA-LAKEHOUSE → PLAT-BI — SQL over JDBC via OAC Data Gateway, OAuth2 service principal.

arch-application.description: Three primary platforms realise the solution, with Oracle CC&B as a read-only operational source.

references.note: Oracle Analytics Cloud 23.x — self-service BI surface. OAC Data Gateway deployed in the fersc AWS VPC to bridge OAC SaaS to the private Databricks SQL endpoint. Hosts the fersc Semantic Model.
Databricks on AWS — bronze/silver/gold Delta tables governed by Unity Catalog. Gold-layer tables exposed to OAC via the SQL serverless endpoint.
Confluent Cloud on AWS — Kafka event orchestration. Schema Registry enforces Avro compatibility. Retention: 7 days operational, 90 days regulatory.
Oracle CC&B 2.9 — primary operational data source via Debezium LogMiner CDC. Read-only; no write-back.

principles-adherence.statement: Ingestion is event-driven by default via CC&B change-data-capture, keeping the non-critical analytics path asynchronous.
The CC&B internal model is transformed and masked at the integration layer before landing in the lakehouse; the source model does not leak into the analytics estate.
Uses the reference medallion (bronze/silver/gold) lakehouse pattern rather than a bespoke pipeline design.

flows-information.title: CC&B to Analytics Cloud Data Flow
flows-information.description: End-to-end sequence showing data movement from Oracle CC&B through the Confluent event backbone and Databricks Lakehouse to Oracle Analytics Cloud and the business user.
flows-information.content:
sequenceDiagram
    participant CIS as Oracle CC&B (PLAT-CIS)
    participant CDC as Debezium CDC Connector
    participant Kafka as Confluent Kafka (PLAT-EVENT-BROKER)
    participant SR as Schema Registry
    participant DBX as Databricks Lakehouse (PLAT-DATA-LAKEHOUSE)
    participant OAC as Oracle Analytics Cloud (PLAT-BI)
    participant User as Business User

    CIS->>CDC: Write billing/account change (LogMiner)
    CDC->>SR: Validate Avro schema
    SR-->>CDC: Schema OK
    CDC->>Kafka: Publish change event (ccb.billing.account.changes)
    Kafka->>Kafka: PII masking transformation (Kafka Streams)
    Kafka->>DBX: Auto Loader consumes masked events
    DBX->>DBX: Append to Bronze Delta table (raw.ccb_billing_accounts)
    DBX->>DBX: DLT pipeline: Bronze -> Silver (cleansed.billing_accounts)
    DBX->>DBX: DLT pipeline: Silver -> Gold (reporting.billing_kpis)
    User->>OAC: Open Operational Dashboard workbook
    OAC->>DBX: JDBC query via Databricks SQL serverless endpoint
    DBX-->>OAC: Return gold-layer KPI rows
    OAC-->>User: Render dashboard with up-to-date metrics

flows-information.title: CC&B Operational Data CDC Flow
flows-information.description: Near-real-time change-data-capture flow from Oracle CC&B to the Databricks Lakehouse bronze layer, covering billing account changes, payment events, and service order updates.
steps: Oracle CC&B writes a billing or account change transaction to its Oracle DB (CC&B schema).
Debezium Oracle CDC connector (running on Kafka Connect) reads the change from Oracle LogMiner and publishes an Avro-encoded change event to the Confluent topic ccb.billing.account.changes.
Confluent Schema Registry validates the Avro schema version against the registered schema for ccb.billing.account.changes.
A Kafka Streams transformation processor applies field-level masking to PII fields (name, address) before routing to the downstream topic ccb.billing.account.changes.masked.
Databricks Auto Loader (Kafka source) consumes events from ccb.billing.account.changes.masked and appends records to the bronze Delta table ops_catalogue.raw.ccb_billing_accounts.

A Databricks DLT (Delta Live Tables) pipeline runs on a 10-minute trigger, transforming bronze records into the silver table ops_catalogue.cleansed.billing_accounts applying deduplication and schema enforcement.

A second DLT pipeline aggregates silver data into the gold table ops_catalogue.reporting.billing_kpis, computing metrics including Days Sales Outstanding, payment failure rate, and unread meter percentage.
Oracle Analytics Cloud queries the gold table via the Databricks SQL serverless endpoint (JDBC) and renders updated KPIs in the Operational Dashboard workbook for business users.

flows-information.title: MDM Batch Ingestion Flow
flows-information.description: Nightly batch ingestion of Oracle MDM meter register data into the Databricks Lakehouse, providing a daily snapshot of the active meter estate for use in regulatory and commercial reporting.
steps: A Confluent scheduled connector triggers an Oracle MDM REST API export at 01:00 UTC, requesting a full snapshot of active meter records.
Oracle MDM returns a paginated JSON response containing meter attributes, location, configuration, and lifecycle status.
Confluent OIC adapter transforms the MDM JSON response to Avro and publishes records to the Confluent topic mdm.meters.snapshot.
Databricks Auto Loader consumes the snapshot topic and overwrites the bronze Delta table ops_catalogue.raw.mdm_meters using REPLACE WHERE partition = current_date.
A DLT pipeline applies MDM business rules (meter type classification, voltage normalisation) to produce the silver table ops_catalogue.cleansed.meters.
The gold table ops_catalogue.reporting.meter_estate_summary is refreshed, providing counts by meter type, region, and lifecycle status for regulatory reporting.

documents.title: CRM Integration Solution Design
documents.description: Logical solution design for the integration between Salesforce CRM (PLAT-CRM) and Oracle CC&B (PLAT-CIS), enabling a unified agent desktop with embedded billing context and event-driven proactive outbound communications.
documents.scope: CRM-to-CIS integration — synchronisation of account and billing data between Salesforce CRM (PLAT-CRM) and Oracle CC&B (PLAT-CIS), mediated by Oracle Integration Cloud.

executive-summary.summary: The CRM Integration solution mediates between Salesforce CRM and Oracle CC&B through Oracle Integration Cloud, giving agents embedded billing context and triggering proactive customer communications.
points: OIC provides synchronous API orchestration for agent account-lookup requests from Salesforce into CC&B.
OIC consumes CC&B billing events via Confluent Kafka to trigger proactive outbound communications in Salesforce Marketing Cloud.
Replaces the existing bespoke Java middleware with a governed, observable integration layer.

context.title: CRM to CIS — Customer Account Sync Specification

capabilities.note: Customer Management — unified agent desktop with embedded billing context.
Retail & Billing — billing account data surfaced to agents and used in notifications.
Regulatory & Compliance — Ofgem Consumer Duty proactive communications.

functional-requirements.requirement: Display a real-time billing summary (balance, last payment date, last meter read, service agreement status) inline within the Salesforce agent's customer record.
Trigger proactive outbound customer communications (email/SMS) in response to CC&B payment failure events, respecting customer communication preferences.
Maintain a cross-reference between Salesforce Account/Contact IDs and CC&B Account Numbers to mediate lookups and event routing.

features.name: Embedded Billing Panel
features.description: Salesforce Lightning Web Component showing real-time CC&B billing summary within the agent's customer record.

features.name: Proactive Payment-Failure Notifications
features.description: Event-driven outbound email/SMS to customers within 4 hours of a CC&B payment failure, via Salesforce Marketing Cloud.

nfr-support-slas.requirement: CC&B payment failure events must trigger Salesforce Marketing Cloud notification dispatches within 4 hours of the originating payment failure event.
nfr-support-slas.rationale: Ofgem Consumer Duty requirement for proactive customer communication.

nfr-business-continuity.requirement: The Kafka consumer (OIC) must process payment failure events with at-least-once delivery semantics. Duplicate suppression must be applied using the CC&B event ID as an idempotency key.
nfr-business-continuity.rationale: A missed payment failure notification constitutes a Consumer Duty breach. Duplicates are preferable to missed notifications but must be suppressed to avoid customer confusion.

nfr-performance.requirement: The agent billing context lookup must complete within 3 seconds end-to-end (Salesforce callout to OIC to CC&B and back) under normal load.
nfr-performance.rationale: Contact centre UX requirement: agents cannot wait more than 3 seconds for the billing panel to render before the call experience degrades.

arch-business.description: Contact centre agents are the primary users of the embedded billing panel. Proactive notifications support Ofgem Consumer Duty obligations by reaching customers quickly after payment failures.

arch-data.description: A cross-reference mapping table (Salesforce Account/Contact ID ↔ CC&B Account Number) is maintained in OIC's lookup store. Customer communication preferences (email/SMS opt-in, language) are sourced from Salesforce at notification time.

arch-integration.description: Two OIC integration flows: a synchronous REST-to-REST account lookup, and an asynchronous Kafka-to-REST flow consuming CC&B billing events and triggering Salesforce Marketing Cloud journeys. OIC mediates all calls and applies idempotency on event consumption.

references.note: PLAT-CRM → iPaaS — synchronous JSON/REST, 10s timeout, OAuth2 client credentials.
iPaaS → PLAT-CIS — synchronous JSON/REST to CC&B Service Layer, 500 requests/minute rate limit.
iPaaS → PLAT-CRM — async JSON/REST to Salesforce Marketing Cloud Transactional Messaging API.

arch-application.description: Salesforce CRM is the customer engagement system of record; Oracle CC&B is the billing system of record; Oracle Integration Cloud mediates between them.

references.note: Salesforce Sales + Service + Marketing Cloud. Lightning Web Component for the embedded billing summary; Marketing Cloud triggers outbound communications.
Oracle CC&B — system of record for billing accounts. Exposes account data via the CC&B Service Layer REST API; publishes billing events via Debezium CDC.
Confluent Kafka — carries CC&B billing events (ccb.billing.events) consumed by OIC.

principles-adherence.statement: Payment failure event consumption uses the CC&B event ID as an idempotency key, honouring the consumer's idempotency contract under at-least-once delivery.
All cross-system calls are mediated through Oracle Integration Cloud rather than point-to-point bespoke middleware.
A 4-hour notification SLA is defined; per-service SLOs and error budgets for the integration flows are still to be formalised.

flows-user.title: Agent Billing Context Lookup — Sequence
flows-user.description: Synchronous sequence for the Salesforce agent billing context lookup via Oracle Integration Cloud to CC&B.
flows-user.content:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Agent as Salesforce Agent
    participant SF as Salesforce CRM (PLAT-CRM)
    participant OIC as Oracle Integration Cloud (iPaaS)
    participant CIS as Oracle CC&B (PLAT-CIS)

    Agent->>SF: Open Customer Account record
    SF->>OIC: POST /cis/account/{accountId}/summary (OAuth2)
    OIC->>OIC: Resolve Salesforce ID -> CC&B Account Number (cache)
    OIC->>CIS: GET /api/v1/accounts/{ccbAccountId}/summary (service account)
    CIS-->>OIC: 200 OK — account summary JSON
    OIC->>OIC: Transform CC&B response to Salesforce billing panel schema
    OIC-->>SF: 200 OK — billing panel payload
    SF-->>Agent: Render billing summary panel in UI

flows-user.title: Agent Billing Context Lookup
flows-user.description: Synchronous lookup of billing account summary from CC&B when a Salesforce agent opens a customer record, providing real-time balance, payment status, and last meter read within the Salesforce UI.
steps: Salesforce agent opens a customer Account record in Salesforce Service Cloud.
A Salesforce Lightning Web Component (embedded billing panel) fires an Apex callout to the OIC REST endpoint /cis/account/{accountId}/summary.
OIC validates the request (service account auth), maps the Salesforce account ID to the CC&B account number via a cached cross-reference table.
OIC calls the CC&B Service Layer REST API GET /api/v1/accounts/{ccbAccountId}/summary.
CC&B returns account summary JSON (balance, last payment date, last meter read, service agreement status).
OIC transforms the CC&B response to the Salesforce billing panel schema and returns it to the Lightning Web Component.
The Salesforce billing panel renders the account summary inline within the agent's customer record view.

flows-information.title: CC&B Payment Failure Proactive Notification
flows-information.description: Event-driven flow from CC&B payment failure event through Confluent and OIC to Salesforce Marketing Cloud, triggering a proactive outbound email and SMS to the customer within 4 hours of the payment failure.
steps: Oracle CC&B records a payment failure on a billing account (direct debit return or card decline).
Debezium CDC connector publishes a ccb.payment.failure event to the Confluent Kafka topic ccb.billing.events with Avro payload including account ID, failure reason, and amount.
OIC Kafka consumer adapter polls ccb.billing.events, filters for event type PAYMENT_FAILURE, and initiates the Proactive Notification integration flow.
OIC queries Salesforce CRM REST API to retrieve the customer's communication preferences (email/SMS opt-in status and language preference) using the cross-referenced Salesforce Contact ID.

OIC calls the Salesforce Marketing Cloud REST API (Transactional Messaging) to trigger the PAYMENT_FAILURE journey with the customer's communication preferences and account details as personalisation data.
Salesforce Marketing Cloud sends the outbound email and/or SMS to the customer within the 4-hour SLA window.
OIC logs the notification dispatch event to the integration audit log for Ofgem Consumer Duty reporting.
